question: Which part of the brainstem sits directly above the medulla oblongata?
explanation: The pons is located just above the medulla oblongata and below the midbrain in the brainstem. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: What is the main role of the medulla oblongata in connecting the spinal cord?
explanation: The medulla acts as a bridge that carries nerve signals between the spinal cord and the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h1)

question: Which prominent ridges on the front of the medulla contain descending motor pathways?
explanation: The medullary pyramids contain the main motor nerve tracts coming down from the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: Cranial nerve X emerges from which part of the brainstem?
explanation: The vagus nerve roots arise from the side of the medulla oblongata along with other lower cranial nerves. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h2)

question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for controlling normal breathing rhythm?
explanation: The breathing control center is located directly inside the tissue of the medulla oblongata. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: A patient with swelling near the brainstem has unstable blood pressure and pulse. Which structure is likely affected?

options.A: Visual cortex in the occipital lobe
options.B: Auditory processing center in the temporal lobe
options.D: Broca's area in the frontal lobe

explanation: The control center for heart rate and blood pressure is located in the medulla. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: What is the name of the center in the medulla that coordinates vomiting?
explanation: The emetic center in the medulla processes signals from the body to trigger vomiting. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of coughing and sneezing reflexes controlled by the medulla?

options.B: Stimulating digestive enzyme release in the gut
options.C: Clearing foreign particles from respiratory passages
options.D: Adjusting blood pH via carbon dioxide retention

explanation: Coughing and sneezing help push dust and irritants out of the airway. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: What is it called when motor nerve fibers cross over from one side to the other in the medulla?
explanation: The decussation of the pyramids is the spot where motor nerve fibers cross to the opposite side. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: An injury in the right medullary pyramid usually causes muscle weakness on which side of the body?
explanation: Because motor fibers cross over in the medulla, damage on one side affects the opposite side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: Why is checking swallowing safety important for a patient with a stroke in the medulla?

options.A: The patient will refuse all medications without prior testing
options.B: It prevents permanent paralysis in the upper extremities
options.C: Swallowing tests measure the exact intracranial pressure level
options.D: Lower cranial nerve damage impairs safe swallowing, risking aspiration

explanation: Medullary strokes can damage the nerves responsible for swallowing, which can cause food or liquid to enter the lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)

question: What is the most important nursing action for a patient with sudden swelling of the medulla oblongata?

options.A: Continuous monitoring of respiratory rate and oxygen saturation
options.B: Encouraging high fluid intake by mouth immediately
options.C: Performing passive range of motion exercises every hour
options.D: Dimming room lights to prevent visual hallucinations

explanation: Because the breathing center is located nearby, swelling in the medulla can quickly lead to breathing failure, making close observation essential. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)
